summary: This bill terminates the Department of Education on December 31, 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill terminates the Department of Education entirely on a fixed date. Eliminating an entire cabinet department directly reduces federal outlays and administrative costs, which aligns with reducing government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, or federal health programs.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border policy, or related enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense budgets or programs.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy programs.
The bill targets the Department of Education, which does not administer core welfare, SNAP, or cash-assistance programs.

The sole purpose of the bill is to eliminate the federal Department of Education, thereby removing federal oversight, funding administration, and regulatory involvement in K-12 and higher education. This directly advances the goal of reducing federal involvement and shifting authority toward states and localities, consistent with school-choice and privatization priorities.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related criminal penalties.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By eliminating an entire department and its associated spending, the bill reduces federal expenditures, which supports efforts to limit deficit growth and prioritize debt reduction.
No provisions directly expand or restrict legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or platform oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
